edits.text: 1. PURCHASE PRICE. At Closing, Buyer shall pay Seller USD 20,000,000 in cash by wire transfer of immediately available funds in exchange for the Shares.

2. CLOSING. Closing shall occur within thirty days after signing, subject to satisfaction or waiver of the conditions to Closing set forth in this Agreement, or on such other date as the parties may agree in writing.

3. REPRESENTATIONS. Seller represents, to Seller’s knowledge and in all material respects, that the financial statements delivered to Buyer were prepared in accordance with the accounting principles stated therein and fairly present the financial condition of the business as of their respective dates, subject to the disclosures made to Buyer before signing.

4. INDEMNITY. Seller shall indemnify Buyer solely for direct losses arising from a breach of Seller’s representations and warranties in this Agreement, subject to the limitations, exclusions, claims procedures, and survival periods set forth in this Agreement. Seller shall have no liability for consequential, punitive, or exemplary damages, except to the extent awarded to a third party.

edits.text:
5. CLOSING CONDITIONS; INDEMNIFICATION.

(a) Conditions to Buyer’s obligation to close. Buyer’s obligation to consummate the Closing is subject to satisfaction or waiver in writing by Buyer, at or before Closing, of each of the following conditions: (i) Seller’s representations and warranties in this Agreement are true and correct in all material respects as of signing and as of Closing (except representations expressly made as of an earlier date, which must be true and correct in all material respects as of that date); (ii) Seller has performed in all material respects the covenants required to be performed by Seller at or before Closing; (iii) all governmental and other third-party consents, approvals, and filings required for the consummation of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement have been obtained or made and remain in effect; and (iv) no law or order of a court or governmental authority prohibits consummation of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement.

(b) Conditions to Seller’s obligation to close. Seller’s obligation to consummate the Closing is subject to satisfaction or waiver in writing by Seller, at or before Closing, of each of the following conditions: (i) Buyer’s representations and warranties in this Agreement are true and correct in all material respects as of signing and as of Closing (except representations expressly made as of an earlier date, which must be true and correct in all material respects as of that date); (ii) Buyer has performed in all material respects the covenants required to be performed by Buyer at or before Closing; and (iii) no law or order of a court or governmental authority prohibits consummation of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement.

(c) Indemnification. Subject to the terms of this Section 5, Seller shall indemnify Buyer solely for direct losses actually incurred by Buyer arising from a breach of Seller’s representations and warranties in this Agreement. Direct losses include reasonable, documented out-of-pocket costs of investigating and defending a third-party claim, to the extent otherwise indemnifiable under this Section. Direct losses do not include consequential, incidental, special, exemplary, or punitive damages, or lost profits, diminution in value, or multiple-of-earnings damages, except to the extent such amounts are actually awarded to a third party in a third-party claim and paid by Buyer. Buyer may not recover more than once for the same loss.

(d) Cap and basket. Seller’s aggregate liability for claims under Section 4 shall not exceed ten percent (10%) of the Purchase Price. Seller shall have no liability for such claims unless and until the aggregate amount of otherwise indemnifiable direct losses exceeds one percent (1%) of the Purchase Price, and then Seller shall be liable only for the amount in excess of that threshold. The aggregate liability of Seller for any breach of a representation expressly identified in this Agreement as a fundamental representation shall not exceed the Purchase Price. The limitations in this subsection apply in the aggregate and are subject to the exceptions in subsection (h).

(e) Survival. Claims for breach of representations and warranties must be asserted by written notice describing in reasonable detail the basis for the claim on or before the date that is eighteen (18) months after Closing. Any representation expressly identified in this Agreement as a fundamental representation survives until the date that is sixty (60) days after the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations. A timely noticed claim survives until finally resolved. Covenants survive in accordance with their terms or, if no period is stated, until fully performed.

(f) Notice and procedures. A party seeking indemnification (the “Indemnified Party”) shall give the other party (the “Indemnifying Party”) prompt written notice of a claim, stating in reasonable detail the nature and, to the extent reasonably ascertainable, the amount of the claim. Failure to give prompt notice relieves the Indemnifying Party of its obligations only to the extent materially prejudiced by the delay. For a claim brought by a third party, the Indemnifying Party may assume the defense with counsel reasonably acceptable to the Indemnified Party by giving written notice within thirty (30) days after receipt of the claim notice, provided that the Indemnifying Party acknowledges in writing its indemnification obligations with respect to the claim, subject to this Section. The Indemnified Party may participate with its own counsel at its own expense. If the Indemnifying Party does not timely assume the defense, or a material conflict of interest exists, the Indemnified Party may defend the claim with counsel reasonably acceptable to the Indemnifying Party, and reasonable, documented defense costs shall be treated as direct losses subject to this Section. The Indemnifying Party shall not settle a third-party claim without the Indemnified Party’s prior written consent if the settlement imposes any non-monetary obligation, admission, or continuing liability on the Indemnified Party, or does not provide an unconditional release of the Indemnified Party; such consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. The Indemnified Party shall not settle a third-party claim for which it seeks indemnification without the Indemnifying Party’s prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.

(g) Exclusive remedy. From and after Closing, the indemnification provisions of this Agreement are the exclusive remedy of the parties for claims arising out of or relating to this Agreement or the transactions contemplated hereby, except for claims based on fraud and applications for specific performance or other equitable relief to enforce this Agreement. Nothing in this Section expands the scope of recoverable losses beyond direct losses as provided above.

(h) Exceptions. The caps, basket, and survival limitations in this Section do not apply to a claim based on fraud. The general cap and basket do not apply to a breach of a representation expressly identified in this Agreement as a fundamental representation; any such claim remains subject to the cap stated in subsection (d). No limitation in this Section applies to the extent prohibited by applicable law.
